body.statement:
The answer to the common-marginal converse question is affirmative.  There is \(c_\epsilon>0\) such that, for every \(n\ge1\), \(m\ge0\), and \(d\ge2\),
\[
R_\epsilon(n,m,d)\ge c_\epsilon
\min\!\left\{1,\frac1n+
\left(\frac{d}{(n+m)\log(en)}\right)^2\right\}.
\]
The dimension-dependent alternatives can be chosen so that the whole random table \(P_{XA}\) has the same law under both priors; consequently auxiliary-only observations create no likelihood discrepancy.
body.proof_tex:
First, the known-marginal experiment is more informative than the finite-\(m\) experiment.  Indeed, from the supplied exact \(P_{XA}\), simulate \(m\) iid auxiliary records, apply any estimator from \(\mathcal T_{n,m,d}\), clip it to \([-1,1]\), and then condition on the labeled sample and \(P_{XA}\).  Jensen's inequality removes the simulation without increasing squared risk.  Hence
\[
R_\epsilon(n,m,d)\ge R_\epsilon^{\mathrm{known}}(n,d)
\ge\frac{1}{512n},                                           \tag{39}
\]
where the second inequality is \(\texttt{thm:known-marginal-boundary}\).

Put \(b_{n,m,d}=\min\{1,[d/\{N\log(en)\}]^2\}\).  If
\(b_{n,m,d}\le C_\epsilon/n\), (39) gives the desired lower bound after changing the constant.  Otherwise apply \(\texttt{lem:auxiliary-invariant-fuzzy-priors}\).  Its target intervals have separation at least \(c_\epsilon\sqrt{b_{n,m,d}}\), its fixed-experiment mixture total variation is at most \(1/2\), and each prior misses its interval with probability at most \(1/8\).  Thresholding any estimator at the midpoint of the intervals and using
\((T-\tau)^2\ge c_\epsilon b_{n,m,d}\) whenever the induced decision is wrong proves
\[
R_\epsilon(n,m,d)\ge c_\epsilon b_{n,m,d}.                   \tag{40}
\]
Finally, for \(a,b\in[0,1]\), \(\max(a,b)\ge\tfrac12\min(1,a+b)\).  Combining (39)--(40) with \(a=1/n\) proves the displayed claim, including the capped constant-risk regime.  The auxiliary invariance is the last assertion of the fuzzy-prior lemma and is exact, not asymptotic.
body.justification: The lower hypotheses preserve the complete random treatment--covariate table, so any discrepancy is gated by at least one labeled outcome mark.
body.gap: A supervised prior that perturbs \(P_{XA}\) is learned by auxiliary records. The new signed construction changes only conditional outcome marks, survives reservoir normalization, and transfers from raw Poisson measures to the fixed two-sample experiment.
body.consumer: The converse prevents planning rules from counting treatment-only records as if they supplied outcome-bearing moments.
